newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen gives Lionda preferential help.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen gives Lionda preferential help.

text.p: Shenzhen Lionda Holdings Co Ltd said it had been granted final approval by the Shenzhen city government to receive preferential treatment aimed at supporting the firm's development.

Lionda, a property, brewing and industrial conglomerate in which the state has a majority holding, said in a notice published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times that it would receive help from the city in a number of areas.

The company said it believed the assistance, in credit, asset restructuring, the reduction of liabilities and the acquisition of other firms, would "play a key role in speeding up its development in the future".

A company spokeswoman recently told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that the concessionary package was part of a programme by Shenzhen to help the city's top state-owned firms become more competitive.

Lionda said in its interim report that under Chinese accounting standards, it had net earnings of 23.66 million yuan in the first half of this year, compared with 34.58 million yuan in the year-earlier period.
The company attributed the earnings slide to a steep drop in its investment returns, which fell to 29.69 million yuan from 34.88 million yuan in the first half of 1995.

Lionda's after-tax profits for 1995 plunged 82.8 percent from the previous year's level of 117.31 million yuan. The firm said that under Chinese accounting standards, it had after-tax profits of 20.13 million yuan in 1995.
